title: Chest pain or pressure
draft: From the medical lead's workbook: educational flow adapted from terrestrial guidance; protocol validation pending crew medical authority. The app prescribes no drugs, doses, oxygen or IV.

steps.text: New chest pain reported. STOP exercise/EVA preparation, stabilize/secure the crewmember, and summon the crew medical officer now. Start event log.
steps.note: Do not wait for sensor confirmation; this is a training/demo protocol.

steps.text: Is the crewmember responsive to voice or touch?
steps.check: Is the crewmember responsive to voice or touch?

steps.text: Any red flags: crushing/pressure-type pain, pain radiating to arm/jaw/back, shortness of breath, cold sweat, fainting, severe weakness, or worsening/persistent discomfort?
steps.check: Any red flags: crushing/pressure-type pain, pain radiating to arm/jaw/back, shortness of breath, cold sweat, fainting, severe weakness, or worsening/persistent discomfort?
steps.note: No red flags does not exclude serious causes.

steps.text: HIGH PRIORITY: Continue immediate onboard medical assessment. Notify flight surgeon NOW through the earliest channel; do not delay onboard care for Earth response. Follow approved crew medical kit/ECG/atmosphere procedures and suspend EVA.
steps.urgency: Flight surgeon now + crew medical response
steps.note: No drugs, doses, oxygen, IV or device-specific therapy prescribed by app.

steps.text: New unexplained chest pain still requires crew medical evaluation now. Keep the crewmember resting and supported; pause critical duties. Assess vitals only with available validated instruments.
steps.note: Do not auto-clear because the pulse/SpO2 appears normal.

steps.text: Is pain ongoing, recurring, or worsening, OR have new red-flag symptoms appeared?
steps.check: Is pain ongoing, recurring, or worsening, OR have new red-flag symptoms appeared?
steps.note: Crew retains responsibility for clinical evaluation.

steps.text: Pain has eased, but the case is NOT automatically cleared. Document timing and symptoms, continue crew medical evaluation and request flight-surgeon review as appropriate. EVA/critical-task return requires authorized clearance.
steps.urgency: Crew assessment; further escalation per medical officer
steps.note: A resolved episode can still be clinically serious.

red_flags: Blood oxygen (SpO2) in the danger range
Heart rate in the danger range (very fast or very slow)
_note: Sensors never answer a step or move the crew on: red flags only light up (Integration & Safety: human assessment > sensors). Old red_flag_routes (5 s auto-route to CPR) removed Nov 15.
